input.original_title: DOGE Uses Social Security Data to Purge Voter Rolls

existing.title: DOGE Uses Social Security Data to Purge Voter Rolls
existing.description_short: DOGE Uses Social Security Data to Purge Voter Rolls
existing.description_long: In March 2025, DOGE employees embedded at the Social Security Administration secretly contacted an unnamed political advocacy group — aligned with True the Vote — and signed a 'Voter Data Agreement' to match SSA records against state voter rolls to 'find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain States.' A DOGE staffer executed the agreement on March 24, 2025, the same day a federal court ordered all DOGE access to SSA data terminated. DOJ admitted in a January 2026 court filing that SSA employees had shared data through an unauthorized Cloudflare server from March 7–17, 2025, and the agency could not determine what was transmitted. By August 2026, DHS's SAVE system had run at least 67 million voter registrations through federal citizenship databases, flagging tens of thousands as potential noncitizens, with some states suspending voter registrations within 30 days of notification.

existing.title: Title X Family Planning Freeze: 879 Clinics, 834,000 Patients at Risk
existing.description_short: Title X Family Planning Freeze: 879 Clinics, 834,000 Patients at Risk
existing.description_long: On March 31, 2025, the Trump administration froze Title X family planning funding for 16 of 86 grantees, withholding more than $65 million that had been earmarked for contraception, STI testing, and cancer screenings at clinics serving low-income and uninsured patients. All nine Planned Parenthood federation affiliates with Title X grants were affected, as were seven other nonprofit grantees. KFF estimated 879 clinics in 23 states — 24% of all Title X clinics — were impacted, and up to 834,000 people could lose access to Title X-funded care. HHS cited unspecified civil rights violations and Trump's executive order barring benefits to undocumented immigrants but refused to detail the alleged infractions. By late April 2025, dozens of clinics had begun closing. Title X serves 2.8 million clients annually across nearly 4,000 clinics, with 83% of patients having family incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty level.

input.original_title: Tom Homan Spreads Misleading 600,000 Criminal Immigrants Statistic

existing.title: Tom Homan Spreads Misleading 600,000 Criminal Immigrants Statistic
existing.description_short: Tom Homan Spreads Misleading 600,000 Criminal Immigrants Statistic
existing.description_long: Beginning July 7, 2025, Trump's border czar Tom Homan repeatedly claimed at public events — including the Turning Point USA Student Action Summit on July 12 and on Fox News — that over 600,000 illegal aliens with criminal records were walking the streets of this nation. FactCheck.org documented extensive flaws: the 647,572 figure from a 2024 ICE letter to Congress included legal immigrants, not just undocumented ones; approximately one-third (222,141) had only been charged, not convicted; roughly 126,000 had only traffic offenses and 92,000 had only immigration offenses; the data spanned 40-plus years of entrants, not recent arrivals; and an undetermined number were already incarcerated by other agencies. Trump himself had separately claimed Biden let in 13,099 convicted murderers, then shifted to 11,888 murderers — numbers drawn from the same dataset but excluding the 40-year timeframe caveat. Reuters data showed ICE detentions of people with no criminal charges jumped 800% under Trump, from approximately 860 in January to 7,800 by June 2025, undercutting the crime-focused messaging.

input.original_title: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote

existing.title: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote
existing.description_short: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote
existing.description_long: In March 2025, two DOGE staffers embedded at the Social Security Administration were contacted by a political advocacy group widely identified as True the Vote seeking to analyze state voter rolls using SSA data to find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain States. One DOGE staffer signed a Voter Data Agreement on March 24, 2025, in his capacity as an SSA employee without the knowledge or approval of SSA leadership or review through proper data exchange procedures. The arrangement was not discovered until November 2025, when an internal SSA audit uncovered it. The SSA made two Hatch Act referrals to the U.S. Office of Special Counsel in late December 2025. The Trump administration admitted to these facts in a January 16, 2026, court filing in a lawsuit by the AFL-CIO. Separately, DOGE staff shared SSA data through an unapproved third-party Cloudflare server and transmitted a password-protected file containing personal information on roughly 1,000 individuals to senior DOGE adviser Steve Davis. SSA whistleblower Charles Borges alleged that DOGE staffers also copied a dataset of more than 300 million Americans' information into an unsecured cloud server.

input.original_title: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops

existing.title: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops
existing.description_short: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops
existing.description_long: Leo Garcia Venegas, a U.S. citizen and Alabama construction worker, was detained by immigration agents three separate times through May 2026. The first incident in mid-2025 involved agents tackling him while he filmed his brother's arrest at a construction site, ignoring his citizenship claims. A few weeks later, an officer at a home he was building refused to trust his Alabama REAL ID — which only citizens and legal residents can obtain. Videos went viral; Garcia Venegas testified before Congress and filed a federal lawsuit. Despite the pending lawsuit, he was detained a third time in May 2026. The same week, masked agents in the Bronx tackled an American teenager who, once identified as a citizen, was left bloody and bruised in an unfamiliar neighborhood. ProPublica reported that in response to its coverage, ICE official Todd Lyons acknowledged citizen detentions serve as a deterrent. His attorney argued the stops constitute racial profiling stops based on the Supreme Court's fall 2024 ruling permitting stops partly based on apparent ethnicity, job in construction, and speaking Spanish. Despite three documented detentions, ICE denied his damage claim in April 2026 with no explanation, then detained him again two weeks later.

input.original_title: DOJ Realignment - 'Fundamental' Policy Shift Away from Corporate Oversight

existing.title: DOJ Realignment - 'Fundamental' Policy Shift Away from Corporate Oversight
existing.description_short: DOJ Realignment - 'Fundamental' Policy Shift Away from Corporate Oversight
existing.description_long: Donald Trump's Justice Department underwent 'fundamental realignment' of operations and enforcement priorities under Attorney General Pam Bondi, who issued 'more than a dozen policy memoranda' that dramatically shifted DOJ away from corporate investigations and enforcement toward protecting business interests while targeting political opponents. The February 2025 realignment included freezing Foreign Corrupt Practices Act enforcement for 180 days while Bondi directed the Civil Rights Division to pursue 'criminal investigations' of companies with diversity programs, representing what legal experts called a 'seismic shift in DOJ's approach to corporate investigations and enforcement.' The systematic policy changes de-emphasized corporate accountability while redirecting prosecutorial resources toward Trump's political agenda, with the administration treating corporate corruption investigations as lower priorities than pursuing diversity programs and political opponents. Bondi's memoranda 'fundamentally realigned DOJ's operations' by protecting corporations from oversight while weaponizing civil rights laws against businesses that maintained diversity initiatives, creating a two-tiered justice system that favored Trump's allies and donors. The realignment demonstrated unprecedented political capture of the Justice Department, transforming the nation's premier law enforcement agency from protector of public interests into a tool for advancing Trump's business-friendly agenda while persecuting political opponents through prosecutorial power. The policy shift created dangerous precedent for future administrations to use DOJ as a weapon of political and economic favoritism rather than independent enforcer of federal law.

input.original_title: Election Certification Interference - Training Trump Supporters to Block Results

existing.title: Election Certification Interference - Training Trump Supporters to Block Results
existing.description_short: Election Certification Interference - Training Trump Supporters to Block Results
existing.description_long: Donald Trump and his allies systematically trained supporters across battleground states to pressure local election officials into refusing to certify election results, creating a coordinated infrastructure to steal elections through procedural sabotage at the county level. Law professor David Clements, a prominent election fraud conspiracy theorist, organized events with thousands of attendees across more than 40 counties in over a dozen states, including critical battlegrounds like Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania, teaching Trump supporters how to intimidate certification officials. The training sessions focused on exploiting the ministerial duty of certification by encouraging Trump supporters to claim fraud without evidence and demand that county commissioners refuse to certify results, potentially disenfranchising entire counties. State election officials responded by issuing stern warnings that certification is mandatory, with Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes stating that counties failing to certify 'risk facing indictment.' The interference campaign built on lessons from 2020, when some Trump-supporting election officials attempted to delay or refuse certification before ultimately being forced to comply with their legal duties. Federal and state courts had already ruled that certification is a ministerial function that election officials cannot refuse based on personal beliefs about fraud, but Trump's network continued training supporters to pressure officials into violating these legal requirements. The systematic training represents an unprecedented attempt to steal elections through coordinated local-level sabotage of the certification process.
